examples.en: On weekends I grill meat on the grill in the yard.

examples.ko: 바람이 불어서 그릴에 불을 붙이기 어려워요.
examples.en: It's windy, so it's hard to light the grill.
This grill is easy to clean, so I like it.
I borrowed a big grill at the campsite.

examples.ko: 그릴 위에서 소시지가 맛있게 익고 있어요.
examples.en: Sausages are cooking nicely on the grill.
The grill is hot, so don't touch it.

explain: 캠핑이나 마당에서 고기를 굽는 기구는 '그릴'이라고 하고, 식당의 불판은 '불판', 생선을 굽는 철망은 '석쇠'라고 해요. 동사는 '굽다'를 써서 '고기를 굽다'라고 말해요. 같은 도구를 '바비큐 그릴'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: The device for grilling meat while camping or in a yard is '그릴'; a restaurant's hot plate is '불판' and a wire rack for fish is '석쇠'. The verb is '굽다', as in '고기를 굽다'. The same tool is also called '바비큐 그릴'.

examples.en: If you eat a lot of sweets, your teeth rot.
I prefer salty snacks to sweet ones.
Lately I keep craving sweet things.
The doctor told me to cut down on sweets.
When I'm stressed, I end up reaching for sweets first.

examples.ko: 저는 단것에 약해서 케이크를 보면 못 참아요.
examples.en: I have a weakness for sweets, so I can't resist cake.

explain: 과자, 사탕, 케이크처럼 단 음식을 두루 가리키는 말이고, 한 단어라서 붙여 써요. '단것이 당기다'처럼 말하고, 소리 나는 대로는 [단걷]이에요. 반대로 짠 음식은 '짠 것'이라고 띄어 써요.
explain_en: It covers sweet foods in general, such as cookies, candy and cake, and is written as one word. A common phrase is '단것이 당기다' (to crave sweets), and it sounds like [단걷]. For salty food you say '짠 것' with a space.

examples.en: I dropped the cup and it shattered all over the floor.
Be careful not to drop your phone.
I accidentally dropped my key into the water.

examples.ko: 접시를 떨어트릴까 봐 두 손으로 들었어요.
examples.en: I held the plate with both hands in case I dropped it.
I was startled by the sound of a book being dropped.

examples.ko: 지갑을 떨어트린 줄 모르고 계속 걸었어요.
examples.en: I kept walking without knowing I'd dropped my wallet.

explain: '떨어뜨리다'와 같은 뜻으로 쓰는 복수 표준어예요. 물건이 저절로 떨어지면 '떨어지다', 내가 떨어지게 하면 '떨어트리다'예요. 그래서 '컵이 떨어졌어요'와 '컵을 떨어트렸어요'는 말하는 방식이 달라요.
explain_en: It is a standard variant form of 떨어뜨리다. When something falls by itself it is 떨어지다, and when you make it fall it is 떨어트리다. So '컵이 떨어졌어요' and '컵을 떨어트렸어요' frame the event differently.

examples.ko: 해가 지면 바닷바람 때문에 훨씬 추워져요.
examples.en: After sunset it gets much colder because of the sea breeze.
The sea breeze is cool and it makes me feel good.
I walked along the beach in the sea breeze.

examples.ko: 해안 마을은 바닷바람 덕분에 빨래가 빨리 말라요.
examples.en: Thanks to the sea breeze, laundry dries fast in coastal towns.
The sea breeze made a mess of my hair.
The sea breeze has a slightly salty smell.

explain: '바람을 맞다'처럼 '바닷바람을 맞다'라고 많이 말해요. 비슷하게 '산바람', '강바람'도 있어요. 조금 딱딱하게 말하면 '해풍'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: People often say '바닷바람을 맞다', like '바람을 맞다'. Similar words include '산바람' and '강바람'. In a more formal register, it is also called '해풍'.

examples.ko: 이 집에는 빈방이 두 개 있어요.
examples.en: This house has two empty rooms.
I lent the empty room to a friend.
If you have a vacant room, I'd like to stay just one night.
A strange noise came from the empty room.
I'm using the spare room as storage for now.

examples.ko: 빈방 하나 보여 주실 수 있어요?
examples.en: Could you show me one of the vacant rooms?

explain: '비다'의 관형형 '빈'과 '방'이 붙은 말이에요. 숙소에서는 '남는 방'이라고도 하고, 집이나 건물이 비어 있는 상태는 '공실'이라고 해요. 사람이 없는 방도, 물건 없이 쓰지 않는 방도 모두 '빈방'이에요.
explain_en: It joins '빈', the modifier form of '비다', with '방'. At lodgings people also say '남는 방', and a vacant property is called '공실'. A room with nobody in it, or a spare room that isn't used, can both be '빈방'.

examples.en: There are lots of persimmons in the yard of Grandma's country house.
Meals at a country house are simple, but you can feel the warmth.
At Chuseok, the whole family goes down to the country house.
After resting a few days at the country house, my body feels lighter.
The country house was old, so we fixed the roof anew.
Every vacation I go to the country house and play with my cousins.

explain: 서울에서 지방으로 갈 때는 '내려가다'를 써서 '시골집에 내려가다'라고 말해요. 부모님이나 조부모님이 사는 집이면 '고향집', '본가'라고도 해요. 명절 때 많이 나오는 말이에요.
explain_en: When you go from Seoul out to the provinces, Koreans use '내려가다' (go down), as in '시골집에 내려가다'. If it is where your parents or grandparents live, you can also say '고향집' or '본가'. It comes up a lot around the holidays.

examples.en: My glasses lenses are cloudy, so I can't see well.
I fell on the stairs and my lens cracked.

examples.ko: 안경알을 닦을 때는 부드러운 천을 쓰세요.
examples.en: Use a soft cloth when you wipe your lenses.

examples.ko: 안경점에서 테는 그대로 두고 안경알만 바꿨어요.
examples.en: At the optician's I kept the frame and changed only the lenses.
My prescription is strong, so the lenses are thick.
I got rained on, and water drops formed on my lenses.

explain: 안경 전체는 '안경', 틀은 '안경테'라고 해요. 안경점에서는 '렌즈'라고도 하지만 일상에서는 '안경알'도 많이 써요. '안경알을 닦다·바꾸다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: The whole pair is '안경' and the frame is '안경테'. At an optician's you may also hear '렌즈', but in daily life '안경알' is commonly used. You say '안경알을 닦다' (wipe) or '바꾸다' (replace).

examples.en: The exam is today or tomorrow, so I'm nervous all the time.
I'll check and get back to you within today or tomorrow.
I heard it will keep raining today and tomorrow.
I'm a bit busy today and tomorrow because I have appointments.

examples.ko: 이 책은 오늘내일 안에 다 읽을 수 있어요.
examples.en: I can finish this book within a day or two.
They said the package I ordered will arrive today or tomorrow.

explain: '오늘이나 내일'을 한 단어처럼 붙여서 아주 가까운 때를 말해요. 정확한 날짜를 모르지만 곧이라는 느낌이라 '오늘내일 중으로'를 자주 써요. 더 넓게 말하려면 '이삼일'이나 '요 며칠'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: The baby's due date is near, so it could be any day now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 곧 큰일이 일어날 것 같을 때 써요. 출산처럼 기다리는 일이 임박했을 때 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something important is about to happen very soon, such as waiting on a baby's birth.

explain_en: It joins 'today or tomorrow' into one word to mean a very near time. It suggests 'very soon' without a firm date, so '오늘내일 중으로' (within today or tomorrow) is common. For a wider span, say '이삼일' (two or three days) or '요 며칠' (these few days).

examples.en: On Christmas Eve, I eat cake with my family.
I hope it snows on Christmas Eve.
I decided to meet my friends on the evening of Christmas Eve.
We first met on Christmas Eve.
It is Christmas Eve, so there are many people on the street.
Reservations for Christmas Eve are already full.

explain: 12월 24일을 말하고, 줄여서 그냥 '이브'라고도 해요. 한국에서는 크리스마스 당일만큼 이브에도 약속을 잡거나 모임을 하는 사람이 많아요.
explain_en: It means December 24th and is often shortened to just '이브'. In Korea many people make plans or hold gatherings on the eve as much as on Christmas Day itself.

examples.en: I squirt tomato ketchup on my fries and eat them.
We are almost out of tomato ketchup.
I drew a heart on the omelet rice with tomato ketchup.
Sorry, could you give me a little more tomato ketchup?

examples.ko: 아이들은 소시지를 토마토케첩에 듬뿍 찍어 먹어요.
examples.en: The kids dip their sausages generously in tomato ketchup.
I got tomato ketchup on my clothes, so I have to wash them.

explain: 일상에서는 줄여서 그냥 '케첩'이라고 해요. 찍어 먹을 때는 '찍다', 짜서 뿌릴 때는 '뿌리다'나 '짜다'와 같이 써요.
explain_en: In daily talk it is usually shortened to just '케첩'. Use '찍다' for dipping and '뿌리다' or '짜다' for squirting it on.

examples.en: My father put film into the old camera.
Film photos have warm colors, so I like them.

examples.ko: 이 필름은 한 통에 서른여섯 장이 나와요.
examples.en: This roll of film gives thirty-six shots.
I put a protective film on my phone screen.

examples.ko: 필름이 다 떨어져서 가게에 가야 해요.
examples.en: I ran out of film, so I have to go to the shop.

examples.ko: 요즘은 필름 카메라를 쓰는 젊은 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: These days many young people use film cameras.

explain: 카메라 필름 말고도 휴대폰 화면에 붙이는 '보호 필름', 창문에 붙이는 '선팅 필름'도 필름이라고 해요. 필름 카메라를 '필카'라고 줄여 부르기도 해요.
explain_en: Besides camera film, the word also covers the protective film you stick on a phone screen and the tint film on windows. Film cameras are sometimes shortened to '필카' in casual talk.
